h1:
Nakhon Pathom Thai Desserts
Don Wai, the Old Market & Local Sweets
intro: Nakhon Pathom has deep roots in Thai sweets, both along the riverside floating market on the Tha Chin River and in the old market that rings Phra Pathom Chedi. Walk a few steps and you'll find pans of hot khanom krok, trays of golden thong yip and thong yot, and khanom tan fragrant with palm fruit. This is a guide to the local desserts that residents actually eat — real shops that are still open right now.

blocks.html: Say Nakhon Pathom and most people picture red pork rice and Phra Pathom Chedi first, but this is really a dessert town at heart. There are two big arenas: Don Wai Floating Market in Sam Phran district, on the Tha Chin River, and the old market and night market around Phra Pathom Chedi in town. The two have very different sweet personalities, so we've covered both sides — and we'll tell you straight which stalls have long queues, which sell out fast, and which sweets travel well as gifts.

blocks.text: Thai desserts you have to try in Nakhon Pathom

blocks.html: Before we run through the shops, let's get to know the sweets that are the stars of this town. Many are old-style Thai desserts that are getting harder to find in Bangkok, but in Nakhon Pathom they're still made fresh and sold day by day.

items.name: Old-style khanom krok with generous filling
items.blurb: The star of the Phra Pathom Chedi night market. Famous stalls like Khanom Krok Je Khaek pile the filling right to the brim — young coconut, taro, corn, pumpkin, purple yam — fragrant with coconut milk, crisp outside and soft inside. Best eaten hot off the griddle.

items.name: Thong yip, thong yot & foi thong
items.blurb: The golden egg-yolk sweets, made from yolks and syrup. These auspicious desserts are something Nakhon Pathom is known for — made fresh and shipped nationwide. When you get a freshly made batch they're sweet and moist without being cloying, and they make a great gift to bring home.
items.meta: Found at both Don Wai and the old market

items.name: Khanom tan (palm cake)
items.blurb: A fluffy golden-yellow cake scented with toddy palm fruit and topped with grated coconut. Pa Khai's khanom tan at Don Wai is steamed fresh every day — soft, fluffy and never dry. It's a shop people make the trip for.

items.name: Khanom mo kaeng (baked custard)
items.blurb: A baked custard sweet topped with fragrant fried shallots — versions with taro, lotus seed or mung bean. It goes well with a black coffee. Central Thailand makes this one well, and Nakhon Pathom has several shops to compare.
items.meta: Sold by the tray or piece

items.name: Khanom chan & pandan dessert sets
items.blurb: Thai dessert shops at Don Wai such as Jerm Thong and Soi Khanom Thai have pandan khanom chan, pumpkin custard, thong yip and met khanun — sliced into small pieces for a few baht each, so you can mix several kinds on one tray.
items.meta: Don Wai · sold by the piece

items.name: Old-style custard-filled bread
items.blurb: Bread lovers won't be let down. At the old market, Tee Cafe does old-style bread with thick custard in several recipes — coconut custard, pandan, pumpkin and butterfly-pea. Over at Don Wai you'll find loaf bread and foi-thong lava cake.

items.name: Khao lam & mango with sweet fish sauce
items.blurb: Sweets to grab on the way home. Grilled khao lam (sticky rice in bamboo) scented with coconut milk is everywhere around the chedi, while mango with sweet fish sauce is a sweet-and-sour snack that pairs perfectly with an evening market stroll.

blocks.title: Before you go
blocks.html: Griddle-fresh khanom krok and freshly made thong yip tend to sell out fast. For the freshest batch, go to the old market in the early evening (5–7 PM); at Don Wai, arrive before 3 PM while the dessert stalls still have everything in stock. Most shops are cash only, so bring small notes.

blocks.text: Don Wai Floating Market — riverside sweets on the Tha Chin

blocks.html: Don Wai sits next to Wat Don Wai in Sam Phran district, about an hour's drive from Bangkok. It's an old riverside market on the Tha Chin River that's busy every day, but weekends are the busiest. It's open roughly 7 AM–6:30 PM. The legendary savory dishes here are stewed five-spice duck and salted mackerel stew, but the dessert side holds its own too — walk along the river and you'll pass a whole row of Thai dessert shops.

items.name: Pa Khai Khanom Tan
items.blurb: Don Wai's famous palm-cake shop — fluffy, soft and fragrant with palm fruit, steamed fresh daily. Plenty of people come to buy it as a gift.

items.name: Jerm Thong Thai Sweets
items.blurb: An old-style Thai dessert shop open late into the evening, with khanom chan, thong yip, pumpkin custard and lotus seed — mix your own selection.

items.name: Pang Pond Don Wai
items.blurb: Crisp, chewy butter bread, custard-filled bread, coconut cake, and the foi-thong lava cake people seek out.

items.name: Soi Khanom Thai
items.blurb: Many kinds of sliced Thai sweets in one shop at gentle prices — perfect for trying several styles.

blocks.html: If you'd rather sit and enjoy your sweets by the water, there are floating cafes in the market where you can order coffee and bakery and watch the boats go by. And if you're after dry edible gifts, Don Wai has sun-dried bananas, mango paste, baked Thai sweets, and Rahong's salted eggs that people buy back by the bagful.

blocks.text: The old market & night market at Phra Pathom Chedi

blocks.html: In central Nakhon Pathom, the area around Phra Pathom Chedi is one of the province's biggest food arenas. The night market runs in the evening, roughly 4 PM–11 PM. The standout sweets are old-style khanom krok with generous filling, traditional Thai sweets, floating ice cream, shaved ice and khao lam. Pay your respects at the chedi, then keep going with a long dessert crawl.

items: Khanom Krok Je Khaek — khanom krok overflowing with many fillings: young coconut, taro, corn, pumpkin, purple yam. Open evening to late, with long queues on weekends.
Tee Cafe old-style bread — bread with thick custard filling in several recipes: pandan, pumpkin, butterfly-pea, taro. Loads of fillings to choose from.
Traditional Thai dessert shops around the market — thong yip, thong yot, foi thong, khanom mo kaeng, khanom chan. Several vendors to taste and compare.
Evening snacks — mango with sweet fish sauce, shaved ice, floating ice cream, fresh fruit. Great for a stroll to settle dinner.

blocks.title: Pair it up to get your money's worth
blocks.html: For dinner at the night market, start with savory dishes — like old-style tom yum noodles or dry sukiyaki — then finish with hot khanom krok and shaved ice. You'll be comfortably full and get to try several shops in one night.

blocks.text: Where to buy Thai sweets as gifts

blocks.html: Many of Nakhon Pathom's Thai sweets make good gifts, but choose the type to match how far you're traveling home. The golden egg-yolk sweets, khanom mo kaeng and khanom tan only keep a few days, while dry items like sun-dried bananas, mango paste, crisp-baked Thai sweets and salted eggs keep longer.

items: Keeps briefly (1–2 days) — thong yip, thong yot, foi thong, khanom mo kaeng, khanom tan, khanom chan. Best eaten within a day or two.
Keeps longer — sun-dried bananas, mango paste, crisp-baked Thai sweets, salted eggs. Good for carrying far.
Easiest places to buy — Don Wai has gift shops lined along the river, while the old market around the chedi has Thai dessert and gift shops in town. Easy to grab before heading back.

faq.q: What Thai desserts in Nakhon Pathom should I try?
faq.a: Old-style khanom krok with generous filling at the Phra Pathom Chedi night market is number one. Next come the golden egg-yolk sweets (thong yip, thong yot, foi thong), khanom tan at Don Wai, and khanom mo kaeng, plus old-style custard-filled bread that you'll find at both markets.

faq.q: Is it better to eat Thai sweets at Don Wai or the old market?
faq.a: They have different personalities. Don Wai is a riverside floating market on the Tha Chin River that's open during the day — good for eating khanom tan and sliced Thai sweets, and for buying gifts. The old market around the chedi opens in the evening and is strong on griddle-fresh khanom krok and street-food sweets. If you have time, go to both at different times of day.

faq.q: What time does Don Wai Floating Market open?
faq.a: It's open daily, roughly 7 AM–6:30 PM, and busiest on weekends. For the Thai dessert and gift shops, arrive before 3 PM so everything is still in stock.

faq.q: When is the Phra Pathom Chedi night market open?
faq.a: It runs from evening into the night, roughly 4 PM–11 PM daily. Khanom krok and most old-style Thai dessert shops start selling around 5 PM, and the freshly made items tend to sell out fast on weekends.

faq.q: Can I buy Nakhon Pathom Thai sweets as gifts?
faq.a: Yes, but choose by how far you're traveling. The golden egg-yolk sweets, khanom mo kaeng and khanom tan should be eaten within 1–2 days, while sun-dried bananas, mango paste, crisp-baked Thai sweets and salted eggs keep longer and travel well.
